segments: [demanded] from him gold as aid to present to the Caliph.
And he also demanded Dubais, the emir of the Ma'addites,
to bring him to the Caliph,
and to win favor with him.
Zangi, however, replied:
"As for gold, I will give you fifty thousand dinars,
and male and female slaves and horses as many as you wish;
but Dubais I cannot give up,
because the command of Sultan Sanjar has reached me
not to surrender him to anyone,
and I cannot transgress his command."
Then Mas'ud, when he was rebuffed,
crossed over and encamped on the west side of Mosul.
And Zangi seized the gates of the city,
and put out all the poor who were unable to survive in a siege,
and he himself fortified himself in the citadel of Mosul.
Mas'ud, however, did not attack Mosul {OCR: ܫܵܘܨܠ},
but went down to Baghdad.
And Malik Mas'ud sent word to the Caliph:
"If you proclaim me,
behold, I am a friend and a servant;
otherwise, you have nothing from me except the sword."
And the forces of Baghdad went out,
and engaged the forces of Mas'ud,
and they routed and were routed.
And while they were in contention,
news arrived that Sanjar
was approaching Baghdad with many forces;
and the people of Baghdad were afraid.
And the Caliph saw
that he was better able to subdue Mas'ud than Sanjar,
and he gave word of peace to Mas'ud,
and brought him in and lodged him in the royal palace;
and they all prepared for war with Sanjar.
And in the year one thousand four hundred and twenty-six [of the Greeks],
526 of the Arabs [1132 AD],
Sanjar came and took Hamadan,
and proclaimed in it Toghril, the son of Mahmud,
the one who was with him.
Then Mas'ud [and] Qaraja, the commander of the Caliph's army, went to Hamadan,
and pursued after the forces of Sanjar.
And they sent word to the Caliph
that he also should go in person to the battle against Sanjar.
And when he had prepared and set out,
news arrived that Zangi and Dubais the Ma'addite had reached an agreement with each other,
and lo, they were coming down against Baghdad.
And because of this, the Caliph returned and entered his court,
and prepared for battle with Dubais and Zangi.
And he went out and engaged them with two thousand [men],
and defeated them.
And Zangi fled to Tikrit,
while Dubais [fled] to the banks of the Euphrates.
